name: Tadasana (Mountain Pose)
summary: Improves posture and body awareness; a calm start to a routine.

name: Vrikshasana (Tree Pose)
summary: Improves balance and focus.

name: Trikonasana (Triangle Pose)
summary: Gently stretches the sides of the body, hips and legs.

name: Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose)
summary: Strengthens the back muscles and opens the chest.

name: Vajrasana (Thunderbolt Pose)
summary: A comfortable seated posture commonly used after meals to support digestion.

name: Ardha Matsyendrasana (Half Spinal Twist)
summary: Improves spinal mobility and may help digestion.

name: Paschimottanasana (Seated Forward Bend)
summary: Stretches the back and hamstrings and quiets the mind.

name: Setu Bandhasana (Bridge Pose)
summary: Strengthens the back, glutes and legs; opens the chest.

name: Marjaryasana-Bitilasana (Cat-Cow)
summary: Gently mobilises the spine and eases stiffness from sitting.

name: Balasana (Child's Pose)
summary: A restful posture that eases back tension and calms the mind.

name: Pawanmuktasana (Wind-Relieving Pose)
summary: Helps relieve gas and bloating.

name: Shavasana (Relaxation Pose)
summary: Deep rest that supports stress and blood pressure management.

name: Viparita Karani (Legs-Up-the-Wall)
summary: A restful pose commonly used for tired legs and winding down.

name: Sukhasana (Easy Pose)
summary: A comfortable base posture for breathing and meditation.

name: Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation, slow pace)
summary: Whole-body movement that raises the heart rate gently.

name: Ardha Kati Chakrasana (Standing Side Bend)
summary: Stretches the sides of the trunk and loosens the spine.

name: Neck and Shoulder Release
summary: Eases tension from long sitting or screen use.

name: Chair Yoga Flow
summary: Mobility and gentle movement for people who find floor poses hard.

name: Deep Abdominal (Diaphragmatic) Breathing
summary: Slow breathing is linked with lower stress and modest blood pressure reduction.

name: Anulom Vilom (Alternate Nostril Breathing, no breath-holding)
summary: Calming breathing practice used for stress and relaxation.

name: Bhramari (Humming Bee Breath)
summary: The humming and slow exhale have a calming effect.

name: Yoga Nidra (Guided Relaxation)
summary: Guided deep relaxation that can help sleep and stress.

name: Mindful Breathing Meditation
summary: Helps manage stress and supports better sleep.

name: Brisk Walking
duration_or_frequency: 30 minutes; 5 days a week (about 150 minutes weekly)
summary: Supports heart health, blood pressure, blood sugar and weight; improves mood.

name: Short Walk After Meals
summary: A short walk after eating helps lower the blood sugar rise after meals.

name: Cycling or Stationary Bike
summary: Low-impact aerobic exercise that is kind to the knees.

name: Swimming or Water Walking
summary: Full-body exercise with very little joint stress.

name: Simple Strength Exercises
summary: Builds muscle and bone strength and helps blood sugar control.

name: Resistance Band Exercises
summary: Safe strength work for older adults and beginners.

name: Desk Break Stretches
summary: Breaks up long sitting and eases neck, shoulder and back tension.

name: Pelvic Floor (Kegel) Exercises
summary: Supports bladder control and recovery around pregnancy and childbirth.

name: Balance Exercises
duration_or_frequency: 10 minutes; 3 days a week or more
summary: Helps prevent falls in older adults.

name: Low-Impact Marching and Step Routine
summary: Indoor activity that is easy on the joints.

name: Gentle Walking in Pregnancy
summary: Helps energy, mood, sleep and healthy weight gain in pregnancy.

name: Active Play for Children and Teenagers
summary: Children and teenagers (5-17 years) are advised about 60 minutes of physical activity a day.

name: Activity Plan for Older Adults (60+)
summary: A mix of walking, strength and balance supports independence and lowers the risk of falls.

name: Balanced everyday eating
summary: Aim for at least 400 g (about 5 portions) of vegetables and fruit a day.; Choose whole grains such as whole wheat roti, brown rice, millets and oats.

name: Lower blood pressure (DASH-style, low salt)
summary: Cut salt at the table and in cooking; use lemon, herbs, jeera and ginger for flavour.; Eat more potassium-rich foods: banana, coconut water, leafy greens, beans, tomatoes (unless your doctor restricts potassium).

name: Blood sugar friendly eating (low glycaemic index)
summary: Choose whole grains and millets (ragi, jowar, bajra) in place of refined flour (maida) and polished white rice.; Fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables and add dal, legumes or other protein.

name: Heart-healthy eating
summary: Use small amounts of unsaturated oils (mustard, groundnut, sunflower, olive) and rotate oils.; Add fibre: oats, whole pulses, vegetables, fruit.

name: Healthy gradual weight management
summary: Use smaller plates and fill half of the plate with vegetables.; Eat slowly and stop when you feel comfortably full.

name: Healthy weight gain and nutrition
summary: Eat 3 meals and 2-3 snacks a day.; Add nutritious energy: nuts, nut butter, milk, curd, eggs, paneer, ghee in small amounts.

name: Easing acidity and heartburn
summary: Eat smaller, more frequent meals.; Finish dinner at least 2-3 hours before lying down.

name: Easing constipation
summary: Increase fibre slowly: vegetables, fruit with skin, whole grains, pulses.; Drink enough water through the day.

name: Soothing a mild cold or cough
summary: Rest and drink warm fluids often (warm water, soups, ginger-tulsi tea).; Gargle with warm salt water for a sore throat.

name: Mild loose motions: stay hydrated
summary: Take oral rehydration solution (ORS) in small, frequent sips.; Keep eating light foods: rice, banana, curd, khichdi.

name: Eating well in pregnancy
summary: Eat regular, balanced meals with extra protein: dal, milk, curd, eggs, paneer, legumes.; Include iron- and folate-rich foods: leafy greens, beans, jaggery in small amounts, fruit.

name: Recovery after childbirth
summary: Eat balanced meals with protein, iron, calcium and fibre.; Drink plenty of fluids, especially if breastfeeding.

name: Nutrition for older adults
summary: Eat small, frequent, nutritious meals.; Include enough protein (dal, milk, curd, eggs, fish, paneer).

name: Healthy eating for children
summary: Breastfeed exclusively for the first 6 months, then continue with safe, age-appropriate complementary foods.; Offer a variety of foods: dal, vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs and grains.

name: Staying hydrated in hot weather
summary: Drink water regularly through the day, before you feel thirsty.; Take ORS, lemon water with a pinch of salt and sugar, buttermilk or coconut water in heat.

name: Good sleep habits
summary: Poor sleep is linked with higher blood pressure, blood sugar and stress.

name: Managing stress
summary: Long-term stress affects sleep, blood pressure and mood.

name: Checking blood pressure at home
summary: Home readings help your doctor decide on treatment.

name: Stop tobacco and cut down alcohol
summary: Tobacco and alcohol raise the risk of heart disease, stroke and cancer.

name: Looking after your feet
summary: High blood sugar can reduce feeling in the feet so small injuries go unnoticed.

name: Regular health check-ups
summary: Early detection makes treatment easier.

name: Healthy posture and screen use
summary: Poor posture and long sitting contribute to neck, back and eye strain.

name: Hand hygiene and infection prevention
summary: Handwashing reduces many infections including diarrhoea and respiratory illness.

name: Safe sunlight
summary: Sunlight helps the body make vitamin D for bones and muscles.

name: Heat safety
summary: Heat illness can become serious quickly.

name: Mental well-being
summary: Mental health is part of overall health, and help is available.

name: Antenatal care essentials
summary: Regular care and knowing danger signs save lives of mothers and babies.

name: Preventing falls at home
summary: Falls are a major cause of injury in older adults.

name: Tracking weight and waist
summary: Tracking helps you see progress and stay motivated.

name: If you are underweight
summary: A low BMI can be linked to poor nutrition or illness.

name: Common cold or runny nose
summary: Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids.; Salt-water gargles may soothe the throat.

name: Mild cough
summary: Warm fluids; honey in warm water for adults and children over 1 year.; Rest and avoid smoke.

name: Mild sore throat
summary: Warm salt-water gargles several times a day.; Warm fluids and rest.

name: Mild tension headache
summary: Drink water, rest in a quiet place and relax the neck and shoulders.; Take a short walk or do gentle neck stretches.

name: Acidity or heartburn
summary: Eat smaller meals and avoid lying down for 2-3 hours after eating.; Cut back on spicy, oily food and strong tea or coffee.

name: Constipation
summary: More fibre (vegetables, fruit, whole grains) and water.; Walk daily and go to the toilet at a regular time.

name: Muscle ache after activity
summary: Rest the area for a day, then resume gentle movement.; Warm compress or a warm bath for stiffness; a cold pack for a fresh swelling.

name: Small scratch or minor cut
summary: Wash hands, then rinse the wound under clean running water and wash gently with soap.; Press with a clean cloth to stop bleeding.

name: Insect bite or itchy bump
summary: Wash with soap and water; apply a cold cloth.; Avoid scratching to prevent infection.

name: Feeling tired after poor sleep
summary: Keep a regular sleep schedule and aim for 7-9 hours.; Get daylight and light activity during the day.

name: Mild loose motions
summary: Take ORS in small, frequent sips.; Continue light food such as rice, banana, curd and khichdi.
